subject: Renewal: pricing & commit rebalance (Nimbus Analytics)
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Carter <lisa@Nimbus.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jan 2027 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Renewal proposal + commit rebalance (initial)

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for the open conversation last week. Per our call, attached is a refreshed renewal package that aims to keep your unit economics predictable while giving you runway for the upcoming product launch. High level:

- Proposal: move from 12-month fixed commit (current) to an 18-month blended-commit with a one-time usage credit to offset the first quarter while you ramp.
- Capacity: +25% reserved capacity in month 1-3, then steady state commit slightly lower than current peak to reduce waste.
- Price hold: we can offer a price hold through the end of Q1 if you sign the SOW by Jan 18.

Files attached: NIMBUS_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf, nimbus_commit_proposal.xlsx (breakdown by month and token band).

Would you be open to the 18-month blended approach if we include a lump-sum credit equal to one month of committed usage? If so I can circulate a DocuSign-ready SOW and loop in Finance for PO terms.

Goal: get an agreement by Jan 12 so we can preserve the price hold and schedule the capacity uplift.

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com

From: Lisa Carter <lisa@Nimbus.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@Nimbus.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Jan 2027 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + commit rebalance (initial)

Sofia —

Appreciate the proposal. A few quick clarifying Qs before we escalate to procurement:

1) Can you confirm the mechanics of the one-time credit (applied as invoice line item vs. prepayment offset)?
2) Is the price hold definitely linked to a Jan 18 signature? Our legal would prefer a later cut-off (end of Jan / Feb) if possible.
3) We need to see the PO-ready SOW for internal approval; do you have a DocuSign link yet?

Procurement is on copy — they will want a clear PO path and a short list of non-negotiables (data residency, audit logs access). I can push internally once we confirm the credit mechanics and the price-hold window.

Thanks,
Lisa Carter
Head of Platform Ops, Nimbus Analytics
lisa@Nimbus.ai

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jan 2027 08:25:00 +0000
Subject: Nimbus negotiation — options and recommended walkaway points

Sofia / team —

Quick internal summary after Lisa's note: procurement will push on the signature window and the form of the credit. Finance can approve a one-time credit (invoice line item) but only if we limit the total to a fixed dollar cap and tie it to an 18-month commit. They also gave a conditional approval for a price hold until 2027-03-31 if we accept a minor uplift in blended price for months 13-18.

Recommended options to present to the customer (ranked):
A) 18-month blended commit + one-month usage credit (invoice credit) + price hold until Mar 31. Finance-approved cap: $48k.
B) 12-month term + 25% reserved capacity uplift + 5% up-front discount (no credit). Faster to close, lower total term.
C) 18-month with tiered rollback (guaranteed min commit) — more complex, pushback likely.

If procurement insists on Feb cut-off, we can extend the price hold to Feb 28 but reduce the credit cap by 20%.

I attached a quick pricing sensitivity (pricing_analysis_nimbus.xlsx) that shows the net ARR and gross margin impact for each option.

Recommend Sofia lead with option A (keeps their economics stable and matches their ramp needs). If they push back on term length, fall back to option B.

Diego
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Carter <lisa@Nimbus.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jan 2027 14:40:00 +0000
Subject: Revised offer (option A) + DocuSign link

Hi Lisa —

Thanks for the quick reply and for looping procurement in. We discussed with Finance and can move forward with Option A AS-FOLLOWS: 

- 18-month blended commit (detailed in attached SOW v4).
- One-time invoice credit equal to one committed month, capped at $48,000, applied to the first invoice after go-live.
- Price hold extended to 2027-03-31 (conditional on SOW signature by that date).
- We will include the standard data residency addendum and audit-log access language in the SOW.

I’ve attached NIMBUS_Renewal_SOW_v4.pdf and pushed a DocuSign envelope (link below) for your convenience: 
https://docusign.com/XXXXX-Nimbus-SOW

HubSpot reference: https://hubspot.com/deal/7421

If this is acceptable, procurement can sign the DocuSign envelope and we’ll issue a final invoice schedule for your PO. Let me know if procurement needs any small redlines — we can usually accept non-substantive PO language without changing economics.

Best,
Sofia

From: Lisa Carter <lisa@Nimbus.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, procurement@Nimbus.ai
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Revised offer (option A) + DocuSign link

Sofia —

Thanks. Procurement reviewed the SOW and asked for one small change: include a payment term of Net 45 instead of our default Net 30 (they have internal vendor cadence). They also asked that the credit show as a contract-level line so it is easy to reconcile against the PO.

Can you confirm you can accept Net 45 and will show the credit as a line item? If yes, we can route to signatures early next week.

Lisa

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Carter <lisa@Nimbus.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Revised offer (option A) + DocuSign link — confirmed

Lisa / team —

Confirmed: Redwood can accept Net 45 payment terms for this renewal and will present the one-time credit as a contract-level invoice line (description: "Introductory commit credit - applied to first invoice; cap $48,000"). I also attached a short summary of final terms (final_terms_summary.docx) for procurement.

Next steps:
- I will update the DocuSign envelope to reflect Net 45 and include the credit line.
- Procurement to sign the envelope; Redwood legal will countersign and we’ll generate the invoice schedule and reserved capacity activation timeline.
- Scheduling: proposed kickoff week of Jan 25 — Diego will own the technical onboarding.

Appreciate the collaboration — excited to keep Nimbus rolling.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia@redwood.com
